recipes.name: Chipotle Cream Chicken
ingredients_raw: 1 pound skinless, boneless chicken breast halves - cut into bite-size pieces

steps.text: Place the flour, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper into a large plastic bag. Close the bag and shake a few times to mix the seasonings, and drop in the chicken pieces, a few at a time. Shake the bag to coat the chicken with seasoned flour.

Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat, and cook and stir the onion and green pepper in the oil until the onion is translucent, about 6 minutes. Stir in butter, and allow to melt. Add the seasoned chicken to the skillet, and cook and stir until the chicken pieces are browned on all sides, about 10 minutes.

Increase heat to medium-high, and pour in chicken broth; stir in the chipotle peppers with adobo sauce. Bring to a boil, and reduce the chicken broth by half, stirring often, about 10 minutes. Remove from heat, stir in the sour cream to make a smooth sauce, and sprinkle with cilantro to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Chipotle Cream Chicken
raw_recipe.description: Tender chunks of chicken breast simmer in a savory, creamy sauce with a smoky chipotle kick. This is great with a side of Mexican rice.

review.reviewBody: I loved this dish. Followed the recipe to the T. When I went to dice the peppers in adobo they were filled with seeds, i did scrape them out and am glad i did. This dish did have quite a bite. Served with mexican rice and flour tortillas. Will definately make this again!

I used boneless, skinless chicken thighs instead of breasts, gluten free all purpose flour, and I steamed some broccoli on top of the rest of the mix during the last 10minutes of cooking. No other changes. Served it over brown rice. Delicious!

This was easy and delicious!! I I changed it to a crock pot meal and really only skipped the breading and frying of the chicken, but added all of the seasonings. It cooked 4 hrs on high setting, then after adding the sour cream and cilantro I turned it down to warm. I also only used one chipotle pepper so my kids might try it, but it was still too spicy for them!! So this is easily adaptable to your needs and tastes.

Great recipe & very close to what I was looking for. I always order this at my favortie Mexican restaurant & decided to try & replicate it at home (its a $20 plate!) rediculous.. I skipped the green peppers & added mushrooms (like they do it @ Gallos). I didn't bread & fry chicken for the same reason I used fat free sourcream. I had the smoker already going so I smoked the breast for a cpl hours before cutting & finishing in my cast iron pot. I cooked everything in one pot & let it simmer for about an hour; only because, as usual, my company was late for dinner. This was so yummy & Im thankful for finding this recipe!

Do not give this recipe a bad review just because you don't like a little flavor and spice. This is HOT. To bring the heat down, add more sour cream. The only few things I did different here, I sauteed the onion and bell pepper separate from the chicken. I then combined everything in a stew pot and let everything simmer for 40 minutes. This was tasty and with tons of flavor. DELICIOUS!

I coated the chicken with a mixture of brown rice flour, chickpea flour, and tapioca starch so it would be gluten free and I had to sub a mixture of bacon grease and sunflower oil b/c my son is allergic to olive oil. I did not chop the chipotles because the recipe didn't say to, and to compensate, I added in about 1 Tbsp extra adobo sauce. I served it to my husband and son without the sour cream, as they are sensitive to dairy, and the rest of us ate it with the sour cream. To be honest, it was a little rich for me, I had a bite before adding the sour cream and preferred it that way. My children did not care for it (too spicy for them, I think), but my husband loved it and at all of his serving and my son's. If/when I make this again, I will omit the sour cream for all of us. Thanks for the recipe!

LOVE this! I use shrimp in this sometimes, instead. My mini food processor (or blender) is very helpful for combining the chipotle peppers, broth and sour cream--though if I don't have sour cream, I just use milk or half and half with water. Yes, this is HOT with the peppers and their seeds, but I am crazy about chipotle peppers in adobe--so to me, this hot is a good thing.

We loved this! Yes a few changes were: double the recipe and serve over cooked large shell pasta. I added 3 Chipotle peppers and sauce. Didn’t have green bell pepper so I used frozen sweet corn instead. Since a few folks here like a little less spice I added 2 cups sour cream for the double recipe. Will make this over and over.

This was easy to make and very yummy. I didnt bread the chicken because i feared it would get soggy before my husband got home. I also added about 1 TBSP of chipotle sauce from the can of peppers because we like spice! I also added a lil bit of flour to thicken the sauce and served over egg noodles. The husband LOVED it.
I added mustard powder, oregano, basil, garlic powder, paprika, thyme, salt, pepper to the flour mixture. I substituted sliced mushroom instead of the green peppers. Served over rice.

Absolutely awesome sauce! Just sautéed onions and diced yellow bell pepper , added the broth, sour cream and chipotles and threw it in the blender. Put it over chicken enchiladas I had made previously and frozen for a later date (without sauce). I usually use canned sauce but didn't want to go to the store so I adapted this recipe. Won't be using the canned stuff EVER again!

I make this recipe fairly often, my kids absolutely love it. The only tweak I make is I add about a tablespoon of brown sugar when I add in the broth and chipotle to round out the flavor. Excellent and easy to make.

I was pleasantly surprised how delicious this is! Chipotle really is a terrific flavor. I didn’t have any sour cream so I substituted it with heavy cream and it turned out great. Quick and easy, and definite recipe to add to your repertoire.

Very good! I’d suggest to use one chipotle pepper and add more if you want more heat. I like heat but its not for everyone. You could add more sour cream if you end up using 2 peppers to balance the heat out.

this recipe is so simple and delicious. We've been making this in my home for years but never thought to put in flour to make it creamy. Its delicious with flour and just as delicious but much healthier without it. 
To save calories I do a mix of flour and corn starch and I slowly add it till it's creamy enough for me. Again, anything go save calories lol.

6 10 17 ... http://allrecipes.com/recipe/218584/chipotle-cream-chicken/ .... Like others said, this was okay, but lacked something; maybe beans, tomatoes, jalapenos. I'm not a firebreather & two weren't really spicy, just smokey flavor that developed into mildly hot as you had more. 'Think it depends how on how much sauce you have with each pepper. I used half the amount of chicken broth & didn't bother with the reducing step; decreased sour cream to 3T. Pretty, restaurant-looking dish. S liked, went back for seconds. K tried a bite & liked. She'd already had spaghetti. :) E hasn't tried yet. For me, three stars, but I"m willing to "play" & S would like it again.

this was delicious I made a few changes I cooked my onion, bell pepper, poblano peppers, fried them in my oil with my chicken, I used poblano peppers because I love them and there not as spicy at the chipotle peppers, then I made my sauce I don't have abobo sauce so I put some soy sauce in a pan with the chicken broth and boiled that then added my sour crème after boiled and poured into the chicken mixture when everything gets tender, this is so a keeper thanks for the recipe

This turned out great! I am very sensitive to spice and this recipe was fine without adjusting the heat. I used two chipotles with seeds. I used plain Greek yogurt instead of sour cream because that's what I had on hand. I served it with an improvised Mexican rice and some guacamole to cool it down.
Loved this Dish!

Made as directed, but didn't use low sodium chicken broth. I scraped the seeds out of the chipotle peppers and the finished dish did still have some heat, not overwhelming, but you could definately tell the devil was in there somewhere. Served with mexican styled rice and corn tortillas. That also helped take some heat off. Maybe should use a little less pepper if cooking for kids. Overall, it's a keeper!
